source_excerpts.text:
LOCAL ACQUISITION AND RARE-CYLINDER STABILITY FOR PRODUCT RESET CHAINS
2026-10-10. Internal constructive theorem candidate, not a novelty or
independent-certification claim. Companion to work/reset_sampler/RESULT.txt.

Model and output claims
-----------------------
Use n two-state coordinates with local flip rates q_i(0,1),q_i(1,0)>0.
There are k active reset channels. Channel j has additive nonnegative
hazard a_j(x)=sum_i a_{ji}(x_i), and on firing replaces the entire state by
an independent draw from the product law nu_j=otimes_i Bernoulli(r_{ji}).
Let a(x)=sum_j a_j(x). Assume known bounds

  0<H_min<=a(x)<=H_max for every x,
  0<q_min<=q_i(z,1-z)<=q_max,
  every positive a_{ji}(z)>=h_min>0,
  b<=r_{ji}<=1-b, 0<b<=1/2.                            (1)

The zero pattern of local hazard entries is known. All k channels have at
least one positive entry. Bounds may be rational and are charged as
numerical condition parameters. In the acquisition corollary, their
inverses/ratios are required to be polynomially bounded, not merely to
have short binary encodings.

Consider a second model with the same local-hazard zero pattern. Suppose
every positive local flip rate, positive hazard entry, and each of the two
probabilities in every reset Bernoulli coordinate differs by a factor in
[exp(-delta),exp(delta)], where 0<delta<=1/4. Both models obey (1), up to
the harmless exp(+-delta) enlargement made below. Define alpha=exp(delta)-1.
There are explicit constants C_TV and C_A, polynomial in n,k and in the
numerical ratios q_max/H_min, H_max/H_min, q_min^{-1}H_max,
h_min^{-1}H_max and log(1/b), such that

  TV(pi, pihat) <= C_TV alpha when C_TV alpha is small,       (2)
  |log[pihat(A)/pi(A)]| <= C_A alpha                    (3)

for EVERY cylinder A specifying any selected coordinates. Formulae for
constants are given below. In particular, (3) remains a relative guarantee
when pi(A) is exponentially small in n. Neither bound contains inverse
stationary probability of a reset label, inverse pi(A), or inverse global
mixing time. Equation (2) also gives bounded-observable error through
|E_pi g-E_pihat g|<=2||g||_infinity TV(pi,pihat).

These stability bounds lead to polynomial-local-experiment acquisition in
the bounded-ratio regime described later. They do not turn the EXACT
stationary sampler for a supplied rational model into an exact physical
sampler for unknown param

ACQUISITION-AWARE STATIONARY FIRST-HIT CDFS
2026-10-10. Internal candidate theorem/proof; no novelty or independent-validation claim.
Companion to RESULT.txt. This note accounts for local parameter acquisition and
physical observation time instead of treating product-chain parameters as free.

Main stability theorem
----------------------
Let Q and Qhat be two finite reversible continuous-time chains on the same
state space and with the same nonempty target B. Write pi, pihat for their
stationary probabilities, m_x=pi(x), mhat_x=pihat(x), and c_xy=pi(x)Q_xy,
chat_xy=pihat(x)Qhat_xy for their undirected edge conductances. Assume the two
chains have the same possible edges and, for some kappa,rho>=0,

  exp(-kappa)<=mhat_x/m_x<=exp(kappa) for every x,
  exp(-rho)<=chat_xy/c_xy<=exp(rho) for every edge.       (1)

Start each chain in its OWN stationary law. If F and Fhat are the CDFs of
first hitting B, including the time-zero atom, then

  sup_{t>=0}|Fhat(t)-F(t)|
       <= 2[exp(kappa)-1]+[exp(rho)-1]/2.                 (2)

The right side can of course be capped at one. It has no dependence on the
stationary target mass pi(B), the killed spectral gap, the cardinality of the
state space, the time t, or the numerical waiting time. For kappa,rho<=1 it
is at most 4kappa+rho. This is a stationary-start assertion; arbitrary
nonstationary starts need separate assumptions and may have much larger
condition numbers.

Proof of (2) by interpolating masses and conductances
-----------------------------------------------------
Put C=B^c and extend any function on C by zero on B. Let M and Mhat be the
diagonal matrices of m_x and mhat_x restricted to C. Let L and Lhat be the
killed Dirichlet matrices, defined by

  u^T L v = sum_{unordered edges {x,y}} c_xy
                         [u(x)-u(y)][v(x)-v(y)],       (3)

with the zero extensions used on B. For theta in [0,1], interpolate the
FULL-state masses and conductances linearly: m_theta=(1-theta)m+theta mhat,
c_theta=(1-theta)c+theta chat. They define a valid reversible CTMC with
generator Q_theta(x,y)=c_theta(x,y)/m_theta(x) for x!=y and row sums zero.
Although this intermediate chain need not be a product chain, it is used
only in the proof. Its killed matrices are M_theta=(1-theta)M+theta Mhat and
L_theta=(1-theta)L+theta Lhat.

Let u_theta(t)=exp(-t M_theta^{-1}L_theta)1_C. Probabilistically,
u_theta(t,x)=P_x^{theta
